card.name: Dainichido Bugaku
card.tagline: Sacred New Year masked dances of Hachimantai, performed at dawn
card.profile: Dainichido Bugaku is a set of sacred ritual masked dances and music performed every 2 January from dawn to noon at Ohirumemuchi Shrine (commonly called Dainichido) in the Hachimantai district of Kazuno, Akita Prefecture, as a prayer for New Year happiness and good harvests (Wikipedia; UNESCO). According to legend, travelling bugaku performers of the imperial court visited in the early eighth century during the shrine's reconstruction and taught the dances to locals; the tradition is now transmitted by elders to the young within four communities - Osato, Azukisawa, Nagamine and Taniuchi - and includes masked dances (with the lion-like shishi) and child dancers. It was interrupted for nearly sixty years in the late 18th century before being revived.
card.insight: UNESCO inscribed Dainichido Bugaku on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2009; UNESCO notes the restored tradition is 'the spiritual core of [the community's] solidarity.'
